items.title: Move Andhra Pradesh HC: Delhi High Court rejects PIL against closure of old Visakhapatnam airport
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday rejected a public interest litigation (PIL) petition challenging the closure of Visakhapatnam airport at Dega after commercial operations were transferred to the new Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia asked the petitioner, Gopala Krishna Kosaraju, to agitate his grievance before the Andhra Pradesh High Court. The Bench said that since the dominant cause of action arose in Andhra Pradesh, the petitioner must approach the jurisdictional High Court. "Petition dismissed on the ground of forum convenience. It is needless to say that the petitioner will be at liberty to agitate his case before the jurisdictional High Court," the Court ordered. Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia The old Visakhapatnam airport at INS Dega, which had handled scheduled commercial flights for decades, ceased such operations last month. The shutdown followed the inauguration of the new Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram on August 1. items.title: Bombay High Court grants actress Shruti Haasan interim relief on plea against AI deepfakes
items.summary: The Bombay High Court has passed an interim order in favor of actress Shruti Haasan on her plea seeking directions to restrain the publication of artificial intelligence (AI) generated and other content that violate her personality rights by misusing her image or likeness. Haasan had approached the Court seeking the protection of her personality and publicity rights, which she contended were being violated through AI-generated deepfakes that use her image without permission, manipulated videos, unauthorised commercial endorsements, and unlicensed merchandise. Justice Madhav Jamdar , in an interim order, recognised the severe harm caused by such digital manipulation of one's image and the rapid spread of deepfakes online. "There is substance in the contention raised by the plaintiff (Haasan) that the continuing dissemination of AI-generated deepfakes, manipulated images, chatbots, and other infringing content has caused and continues to cause irreparable injury to the plaintiff's goodwill, reputation, and commercial interests. items.title: Allahabad HC rejects plea questioning Rahul Gandhi's citizenship after petitioner fails to produce evidence
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court has refused to entertain a petition challenging Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi's right to be a Member of Parliament (MP) on the ground that he is not a citizen of India [Ashok Pandey and Another v Sri Rahul Gandhi @ Raul Vinci New Delhi and 2 Others] In its order passed on August 31, a bench of Justice Shekhar B Saraf and Justice Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary noted that the petitioner failed to produce even a single document to prove his allegation that Gandhi was a citizen of the United Kingdom. Considering the Court's observations, the petitioner chose to withdraw the plea. The request was granted by the Court. "In light of the submission made above, the petitioner is permitted to withdraw the present writ petition. The present writ petition as such is dismissed as withdrawn," the Court said. Justices Shekhar B Saraf and Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary Allahabad High Court Petitioner could not show a single document to show that Rahul Gandhi has declared himself to be a British citizen. items.title: ‘Saffron hooliganism’ coverage FIRs: HC asks for no coercive action against Anandabazar Patrika journalists
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court has asked the West Bengal government to assure that no coercive steps would be taken against Anandabazar Patrika journalists facing FIRs over the newspaper’s use of the phrase “saffron hooliganism”, as long as they cooperate with the notices issued to them, LiveLaw reported . The first case was filed on August 28 at the Bowbazar police station in Kolkata over a complaint by Shastri Maharaj, described as a Hindu monk. It objected to the term, ‘gerua gundami’ that translates into ‘saffron hooliganism’ that featured in reports by the publication on violent clashes that erupted at Jadavpur University earlier last month. Several press associations have demanded the immediate withdrawal of the FIRs. On Thursday, the state, represented by the Additional Advocate General Rajdeep Mazumdar, gave the assurance the court asked for after Senior Advocate S N Mookherjee, assisted by Advocates Arunabha Deb and Ashika Daga, flagged the FIRs. Mookherjee reportedly said the cases had been initiated on the allegation of incitement as if journalists had demeaned sanyasis across the country. items.title: Punjab & Haryana High Court quashes dismissal of DSP accused of facilitating Lawrence Bishnoi TV interview
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has ordered reinstatement of a Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) who was dismissed last year by Punjab government for allegedly facilitating a television interview of gangster Lawrence Bishnoi while he was in custody [Gursher Singh Sandhu v State of Punjab and Other] By way of a judgment passed on September 1, Justice Namit Kumar quashed the order by which DSP Gursher Singh Sandhu was dismissed from service under Article 311(2)(b) that allows the State to dismiss an employee without holding a regular departmental inquiry. The Court ruled that the satisfaction recorded by the competent authority for dispensing with the departmental inquiry did not meet the constitutional standard prescribed under Article 311(2)(b) of the Constitution. Thus, it quashed Sandhu's dismissal. However, the Court also clarified that the State can resume an earlier departmental inquiry initiated against him. The enquiry pending before retired Justice Rajiv Narain Raina had been closed after the State decided to dismiss Sandhu without holding any inquiry. items.title: Driving at high speed alone not rash or negligent driving: Delhi High Court
items.summary: Vehicles are intended to be driven fast and the fact that a vehicle was moving at high speed does not, by itself, establish criminal rashness or negligence on the part of the driver, the Delhi High Court recently observed [State v Sanjay] . Justice Chandrasekharan Sudha made the observation while dismissing the Delhi government’s appeal against the acquittal of a tempo driver booked under Sections 279 (rash driving) and 304A (causing death by negligence) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) for causing a woman’s death in a road accident in 2009. “ Vehicles are intended to be driven in speed. Merely because the vehicle was driven at high speed would not mean that the driver was rash or negligent by itself. ‘High speed’ or ‘over speed’ are relative terms, ” the Court said. items.title: India's Got Latent row: Supreme Court quashes FIRs against Samay Raina, Ranveer Allahbadia, others
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday quashed criminal cases filed against digital creator and podcast host Ranveer Allahbadia, and YouTuber-comedians Samay Raina, Ashish Chanchlani and four others over their controversial remarks during an episode of comedy talent show, India's Got Latent. A Bench Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana passed the order. Apart from Allahbadia, Raina, and Chanchlani, the others who have been given relief in connection with this case are Vipul Goyal, Balraj Paramjeet Singh Ghai, Sonali Thakkar alias Sonali Aditya Desai, and Nishant Jagdish Tanwar. The Court today also appreciated the efforts made by Raina, Goyal, Ghai, Thakkar and Tanwar to organise shows for the benefit of persons with disabilities. " Once there are genuine efforts positive results are bound to be there. They are very bright youngsters. If they have started working in positive direction, there will be positive output," the Bench said. The Court proceeded to quash criminal cases filed against Raina, Goyal, Ghai, Thakkar and Tanwar over insensitive remarks made on the show against disabled persons.
